candidates.statement: In section 745A(b)(3) of the FD&C Act, Congress granted explicit statutory authorization to 44 FDA to specify in guidance the electronic submissions requirement by providing standards, 45 criteria for waivers and exemptions, and a timetable for such submissions. Accordingly, to the 46 extent that this document provides such requirements under section 745A(b)(3) of the FD&C 47 Act, indicated by the use of mandatory words, such as must or required, this guidance is not 48 subject to the usual restrictions in section 701(h) of the FD&C Act and FDA’s good guidance 49 practices (GGPs) regulations, such as the requirement that guidances not establish legally 50 enforceable responsibilities. See 21 CFR 10.115(d). 51

Current Electronic Submission Template Structure, 155 Format, and Use 156 The electronic submission template, eSTAR, is the only currently available electronic 157 submission template at this time to facilitate the preparation of PMA/PMA supplement electronic 158 submissions. eSTAR consists of a collection of questions, text, logic, and prompts within a 159 template that guides a user through construction of a ‘complete’ submission. 17 eSTAR is highly 160 automated, includes integrated databases (e.g., FDA product codes , FDA-recognized voluntary 161 consensus standards ), and includes targeted questions designed to collect specific data and 162 information from the applicant. eSTAR also includes applicable links to regulations, relevant 163 guidances, and other resources for the applicant’s reference. candidates.statement: Information Requested Description Market History A brief description of the foreign and U.S. marketing history, if any, of the device, including a list of all countries in which the device has been marketed and a list of all countries in which the device has been withdrawn from marketing for any reason related to the safety or effectiveness of the device. The description shall include the history of the marketing of the device by the applicant and, if known, the history of the marketing of the device by any other person (21 CFR 814.20(b)(3)(iv)).
candidates.context: 25 https://www.fda.gov/medical-devices/device-advice-comprehensive-regulatory-assistance/standards-and- conformity-assessment-program Benefits, Risks, and Mitigation Measures A discussion demonstrating that the probable benefits to health from use of the device outweigh any probable injury or illness from such use ( see 21 CFR 814.20(b)(3)(vi) and 860.7). Data and information in the PMA supporting this should constitute valid scientific evidence within the meaning of 21 CFR 860.7(c) ( see also FDA guidance “ Factors to Consider When Making Benefit-Risk Determinations in Medical Device Premarket Approval and De Novo Classifications ”).

candidates.statement: Labeling Submission of proposed labeling in sufficient detail to satisfy the requirements of 21 CFR 814.20(b)(10). Generally, if the device is an in vitro diagnostic device, the labeling must also satisfy the requirements of 21 CFR 809.10. Additionally, the term “labeling” generally includes the device label, instructions for use, and any patient labeling ( see sections 201(k) and (m) of the FD&C Act and FDA guidance “ Guidance on Medical Device Patient Labeling ”).
